extraction.document_summary: AIA Absolute Critical Cover is a critical illness protection plan that also extends to “every stage” of covered conditions, including early, intermediate and major stage critical illnesses, as well as chronic diseases, age-related conditions, and “future unknown diseases”. Buyers can choose a coverage term “up to age 65, 75, or 100”. The plan pays (i) critical illness benefits for covered conditions (including named examples such as thyroid disorders and sleep apnoea), (ii) an additional Safety Net Cover payout if admitted to ICU for at least 4 days—equal to 20% of the coverage amount on top of existing coverage, with a cap described for this benefit, and it terminates thereafter, and (iii) potential cash value only when the term is “up to age 100” via surrender and maturity benefits (75% of coverage amount; maturity at age 100 is 150% of coverage amount). A key caveat is that claims under the Critical Illness Benefit reduce surrender/maturity benefits, and there are stated exclusions such as pre-existing conditions with waiting/survival periods.
quality_notes: Brochure includes many benefit mechanics and caps (e.g., Safety Net Cover ICU stay, surrender/maturity percentages, booster reset/relapse rules).
Exact underwriting terms, entry age limits, and the full list of plan-specific payable amounts for all conditions are not provided in this excerpt.
The full list of covered conditions appears in tables, but these tables do not provide per-condition payout amounts beyond the special/pre-early categories described.

policies.quick_summary: Future-looking critical illness protection (early/intermediate/major plus pre-early/chronic/age-related conditions) with an ICU Safety Net Cover add-on payout and potential cash value when coverage term is selected up to age 100; claims can reduce surrender/maturity benefits and pre-existing conditions are excluded with waiting/survival periods applying where stated in the brochure. An optional ASCC Booster enables multiple claims via Power Reset/Power Relapse mechanisms; optional premium waiver riders exist for adults and children (named). Eligibility and underwriting details are not provided in this excerpt.
